items.title: Uptake is defined in eleven ways
items.whyItMatters: Pooling studies with different definitions would compare unlike things (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Adopt completed and clinician-reviewed per visit as the core outcome and code every study's definition.

items.title: Durability after support ends is rarely reported
items.whyItMatters: Effects fell back in two studies (claims c2, c5); a purchase decision needs durable effects.
items.opportunity: Extract the latest follow-up after support ends as a separate outcome.

items.title: Older patients and those without smartphones complete less
items.whyItMatters: A phone prompt could widen gaps.
items.opportunity: Extract completion by age and device access where reported.

items.title: Few community mental health settings
items.whyItMatters: Only three of 14 outcome studies were set in community services.

errorsFound: Treating completion of a form as uptake would overstate what prompts achieve; clinician review is the step that changes care.
reevaluation: The review should compare strategies on a harmonised uptake outcome with durability, and treat patient outcomes as a secondary question.
summary: Four gaps: definitions, durability, equity of access to prompts, and setting.
